title: CI/CD & DevOps for SDKs
description: Jenkins, Git, Gerrit, Docker — release pipelines and automation thinking for SDK verification

questions.scenario: Your SDK verification suite is flaky in Jenkins only on shared agents. Locally it is stable. Artifacts show different NIC driver versions across agents.
questions.question: Propose a pipeline design change that attacks the root cause (2–3 sentences).
questions.modelAnswer: Pin a golden container/image (or labeled agent pool) with locked driver/toolchain versions; run the suite in that reproducible environment and fail the job if host/driver drift is detected.
questions.explanation: CI flakes from environment drift are fixed by immutability: containers, labels, version gates — not by retrying forever.

questions.question: In Gerrit-centric workflows, what is a Change-Id primarily used for?
options: Linking patch sets of the same logical review across revisions
Encrypting Git objects at rest on the server
Selecting which Jenkins agent label executes a job
Tagging Docker layers for multi-arch manifests
questions.explanation: Gerrit Change-Id ties amended commits/patch sets to one reviewable change.

questions.question: Write a git command to create a new branch named sdk-verify-fix from the current HEAD.
acceptedAnswers: git branch sdk-verify-fix && git checkout sdk-verify-fix
questions.modelAnswer: git switch -c sdk-verify-fix   # or git checkout -b sdk-verify-fix
questions.explanation: Either modern switch -c or classic checkout -b creates and checks out the branch.

questions.question: Name THREE stages you would put in a CI pipeline for an SDK release candidate (ordered).
questions.modelAnswer: e.g. lint/static analysis → build → unit/integration/HW-in-loop tests → package/sign → publish artifacts
questions.explanation: Leaders expect a clear quality gate order before artifacts leave the factory.

questions.question: Write a minimal Dockerfile that starts FROM ubuntu:22.04, installs python3 and pip noninteractively, and sets WORKDIR to /workspace.
acceptedAnswers:
FROM ubuntu:22.04
RUN apt-get update && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y python3 python3-pip && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
WORKDIR /workspace
questions.modelAnswer:
FROM ubuntu:22.04
RUN apt-get update && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y python3 python3-pip && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
WORKDIR /workspace
questions.explanation: Pin base image, noninteractive apt, install tools, set workdir — CI image basics.

questions.question: What is a healthy approach to flaky tests in a release-blocking Jenkins pipeline?
options: Quarantine/fix root cause with ownership; avoid silent infinite retries that greenwash failures
Increase retries to 50 so the board always stays green
Delete assertions until the job passes
Disable the pipeline on Fridays only
questions.explanation: Managers are judged on signal quality. Retries without triage hide product risk.

questions.question: Explain in one sentence how Docker helps SDK verification reproducibility.
questions.modelAnswer: Containers freeze toolchain/OS dependencies so tests run in the same environment across laptops and CI agents.
questions.explanation: Reproducibility is the product; Docker is a packaging mechanism for that.

questions.question: Write a docker command to run image sdk-verify:1.2 interactively with the current directory mounted at /workspace.
questions.explanation: Interactive run + bind mount is the everyday developer loop for containerized suites.

questions.scenario: Firmware, driver, and SDK teams share one nightly. A late firmware drop broke 40% of SDK tests after merge.
questions.question: As verification manager, what gating policy would you propose between those components?
questions.modelAnswer: Require a compatibility matrix / integration gate: SDK promote only against signed firmware+driver pairs that passed a joint smoke suite; block nightlies from mixing unpromoted drops.
questions.explanation: Cross-team HW/SW orgs need explicit promotion contracts, not hope.

questions.question: What does a Jenkins agent label typically control?
options: Which machines/capabilities are eligible to execute a job
The semantic version of the Git commit message
The MTU of the Docker bridge network
questions.explanation: Labels route jobs to hardware pools (e.g., gpu, nic-lab, x86).

questions.question: Write a short checklist (3 bullets in one answer) for making an SDK CI job “merge-blocking ready”.
questions.modelAnswer:
- Deterministic environment
- Clear pass/fail artifacts & logs
- Timeouts + flake policy with owners
questions.explanation: Merge gates need reliability, observability, and ownership — not just a shell script.

questions.question: In a Jenkins declarative pipeline, write a tiny skeleton with agent any and one stage named Verify that runs sh "pytest -q".
questions.explanation: Declarative pipelines need agent + stages + steps — enough to discuss in interviews.

followUpQuestions.question: What Gerrit field links patch sets of one logical change?
Git command to show the last commit message?
followUpQuestions.explanation: git log -1 or git show reads the tip commit.

followUpQuestions.question: Docker primarily improves CI by…
options: Packaging a reproducible runtime for builds/tests
Replacing the need for any test assertions
Increasing NIC line rate in hardware

followUpQuestions.question: Name one danger of retrying failed CI tests without triage.
followUpQuestions.explanation: Retries can mask real regressions and destroy signal.

followUpQuestions.question: What do Jenkins labels select?
followUpQuestions.explanation: Labels select which agents can run the job.

tutorial.intro: Learn CI/CD by understanding what each Git, Docker, and Jenkins command actually does — and how to design gates that tell the truth.

levels.title: Basics
levels.tagline: Git branches, Docker runs, and a pipeline mental model
levels.html:
Goal: move code through build → test → package with a reproducible environment.

1. Create a working branch

git switch -c sdk-verify-fix
git switch
Change branches (modern alternative to git checkout).
-c sdk-verify-fix
Create a new branch with this name and switch to it.
git status
git status
Show staged/unstaged files and the current branch — always run before committing.
git log -1 --oneline
git log
Show commit history.
-1
Only the latest commit.
--oneline
Compact one-line format.

2. Run tests inside a container

docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace sdk-verify:1.2 bash
docker run
Create and start a container from an image.
--rm
Delete the container when it exits (keeps labs clean).
-it
Interactive terminal (stdin + TTY) so you get a shell.
-v "$PWD":/workspace
Bind-mount your current directory into /workspace in the container.
-w /workspace
Set working directory inside the container.
sdk-verify:1.2
Image name:tag — pin tags (or digests) for reproducibility.
bash
Command to run inside the container.
Why Docker for verification

The same pytest that passes on your laptop can fail on a Jenkins agent with a different driver/Python. Containers freeze the userspace toolchain. (Kernel/driver on the host may still differ — that is a separate pin.)

3. Minimal Dockerfile you can explain

FROM ubuntu:22.04
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y python3 python3-pip \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
WORKDIR /workspace
  • FROM — base image (start from a known OS).
  • ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive — stop apt from prompting in CI.
  • RUN apt-get ... — install tools at build time; clean lists to shrink layers.
  • WORKDIR — default directory for later RUN/CMD.
docker build -t sdk-verify:1.2 .
docker build
Build an image from a Dockerfile.
-t sdk-verify:1.2
Tag the resulting image.
.
Build context = current directory (sends files to Docker daemon).

levels.title: Advanced
levels.tagline: Jenkins agents, Gerrit Change-Ids, flake policy
levels.html:
1. Declarative Jenkins pipeline (what each block means)

pipeline {
  agent any
  stages {
    stage('Verify') {
      steps {
        sh 'pytest -q'
      }
    }
  }
}
  • pipeline { } — Declarative pipeline root.
  • agent any — Run on any available executor (replace with label 'nic-lab' for hardware).
  • stages / stage — Named phases shown in the UI.
  • steps { sh '...' } — Shell commands on the agent.
  • pytest -q — Quiet pytest; still fails the step on assertion errors.
Agent labels

Labels route jobs to machines with the right NICs/GPUs. Without them, hardware tests randomly land on empty VMs and “flake”.

2. Gerrit Change-Id

A Change-Id footer in the commit message ties patch sets of one logical review together as you amend. Interviewers expect you to know reviews iterate without new unrelated changes.

3. Flakes: the management-quality rule

  • Do not infinite-retry until green — that hides product risk.
  • Quarantine with an owner + deadline, keep a minimal honest gate.
  • Track flake rate as an SLO.
Anti-pattern

Marking the entire pipeline optional because it is red. That trains the org to ignore quality.

git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master
git push
Upload commits to the remote.
HEAD:refs/for/master
Gerrit-style refspec: create/update a review for master (server-specific).

On GitHub you’d open a PR instead — same idea: reviewed integration, not direct push to main.

levels.title: Expert
levels.tagline: Promotion matrices across firmware, driver, and SDK
levels.html:
In HW/SW companies, compatibility is a release artifact.

SDK nightly consumes:
  driver_version >= promoted_min
  fw_bundle = promoted/latest-stable
Fail closed if fingerprint mismatches.
  • Promote FW+driver pairs that passed joint smoke.
  • SDK signs off only against promoted pairs.
  • Publish environment fingerprints in every CI artifact.
sha256sum dist/sdk.tar.gz > dist/sdk.tar.gz.sha256
sha256sum
Compute a cryptographic hash of the artifact.
> file.sha256
Save the fingerprint for later verify/reproducibility.
Manager/tech hybrid

“Merge-blocking smoke on golden agents; nightlies expand coverage; promotion contracts stop silent mix-and-match of FW/driver/SDK.”

docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' sdk-verify:1.2
docker image inspect
Show metadata for an image.
--format {{.Id}}
Print the image ID/digest-related id for fingerprinting CI.
